summary: No-ship. R-1 resolved: app discovery no longer filters required artifacts, consumer-side semantics and regression coverage are explicit (lines 39-68, 213-216). R-2 resolved: mirrors are non-authoritative, aliases resolve transitively, and the cron counterexample is corrected (lines 89-127). R-3 resolved: pg-tools has precedence plus a separate CONSUMERS-completeness invariant (lines 132-145). The revision introduces two new high-severity false-green paths.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: G1 treats a vacuous Bats invocation as authoritative enforcement
findings.body: G1 includes every `scripts/verify-*.sh` guard, but recognizes only gate/cron authority and treats guards reached through the required Bats suite as covered. `test_verify-runbook-index.bats` invokes `verify-runbook-index.sh` in CI, where the guard exits successfully because its gitignored runbooks are absent; its effective owner is the owner-local Make target, which G1 excludes. The accounting can therefore pass while the invariant was never evaluated, allowing a local-only guard to lose its real execution path undetected.
findings.recommendation: Define authority as execution against the guard's real domain. Count explicit owner-local entrypoints as an authority class, and classify fixture-, smoke-, or skip-only Bats invocations as non-authoritative.

findings.title: G2 assigns Renovate ownership without proving update applicability
findings.body: The precedence table assigns third-party platform images to Renovate, but Renovate matching is relegated to an approximate, non-verdict freshness report. An `ignorePaths` change, manager-pattern gap, or unsupported manifest shape can therefore leave an image unextractable while G2 still reports an authoritative owner based only on classification. This creates silent stale-pin exposure and also weakens the claimed D-2 detection, which requires proving Renovate cannot reach chart-internal images.
findings.recommendation: When Renovate is the selected authoritative owner, require a blocking owner-specific applicability check. Prefer Renovate extraction or dry-run evidence; otherwise use a fail-closed approximation with sentinel tests, while keeping Renovate non-authoritative for pg-tools and app pins.

next_steps: Add owner-local and domain-effective execution semantics to G1, including a skip-only counterexample.
Make Renovate applicability blocking only for artifacts whose selected authoritative owner is Renovate.
